interface.title: Celestia · Orbital Lab
interface.field: Celestial mechanics / astrodynamics (circular restricted three-body problem)
interface.stage_of_work: Exploration and teaching: what-if simulation and visual inspection of equilibrium stability
interface.what_it_is_for: Pick a two-body system or custom masses, find its five Lagrange points and whether each is stable, nudge a satellite away from one, integrate its path over three orbital periods, and inspect it in rotating-frame 2D, animated and 3D effective-potential views with summary telemetry.

data.note: No data is uploaded. Bodies come from a built-in list (Sun, Mercury, Venus, Earth, Moon, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto) with fixed masses in Earth masses, or 'Custom' with a typed mass. Separation is a slider from 0.10 to 5.00 AU, so real separations such as Earth–Moon (about 0.0026 AU) or Sun–Jupiter (5.2 AU) cannot be set. This hardly matters for the dynamics. The trajectory is expressed in units of the separation, so separation only rescales the orbital period, and the motion depends on μ alone. The map is drawn in these normalised units. 'Max deviation' is labelled AU by the app, but it is in units of the separation (the code divides by separation). The only file produced was a PNG of the plot (plot-image.png).

tree.general: Find the equilibrium points of a two-body gravitational system, judge their stability, and test how a small body behaves when displaced from them
tree.specific: Compute L1–L5 for a chosen primary/secondary pair, read the stable/unstable verdict for each (a fixed rule in the sidebar, an eigenvalue-based badge above the map), offset a satellite from a Lagrange point, integrate the path with REBOUND, and compare libration with escape

children.general: Perturb a test body and simulate its motion
children.specific: Use Position trim and Velocity trim to offset the satellite from the selected point; the app integrates three orbital periods automatically

children.general: Offset the test body's starting state from the equilibrium point
children.specific: Use any of the trims below. Per the code they add together; combining them was not tried in this run. Each change reruns the three-period forecast. Trims run up to ±1.5 (position) and ±1 (velocity) in normalised units, so values like 0.29 are large shifts, not small nudges. Optionally press ↺ 'Recenter probe and zero the perturbations' before the next trial.

features.name: Catalogue-or-custom two-body system picker with derived parameters
features.general: Pick two items from a reference catalogue or type custom values; derived quantities update at once and a reset restores the default pair
features.specific: Primary/Secondary Body dropdowns (planets, Moon, Sun, Pluto, Custom) with M₁/M₂ readouts or Mass (Earth Masses) inputs, a Separation (AU) slider (0.10–5.00), and live Mass ratio μ and Orbital period. Separation only rescales the period, because the path is in units of the separation. ↺ resets to Earth–Moon.
steps: Open the Mission controls sidebar
Choose Primary Body from the dropdown, or Custom and type Mass 1
Choose Secondary Body, or Custom and type Mass 2
Drag Separation (AU)
Read Mass ratio μ, and (after selecting a Lagrange point) Orbital period in telemetry
Optionally press ↺ to reset to Earth–Moon
serves_tasks: Choose the two massive bodies from a catalogue and read off the derived mass ratio and period
Enter an arbitrary mass for one body instead of a catalogue value
Set the distance between the two bodies

features.name: Equilibrium point selector with stability verdict
features.general: Pick one of several computed equilibrium points and see a stable/unstable verdict; the chosen point is highlighted on the map and becomes the start of the simulation
features.specific: 'Select Lagrange Point' radio buttons (L1–L5) drive a sidebar alert ('L1 is an unstable saddle point' / 'L4 region is stable'), a badge above the map, a ring around the chosen diamond, and the satellite's start position. Per the code, the sidebar alert is a fixed rule: L1–L3 are always unstable, and L4/L5 are stable when μ < 0.038521. Only the badge comes from eigenvalues. For an unstable L5 the badge wrongly reads 'UNSTABLE SADDLE'.
steps: Set up the system
Click a Lagrange point radio (L1–L5)
Read the stability alert and the map badge
See the satellite ring placed on the chosen point
Change μ and check whether the verdict flips
serves_tasks: Classify each equilibrium point as stable or unstable
See where all equilibrium points lie for the current system

features.name: Perturb-and-rerun trim panel
features.general: Offset a test particle's starting position (x and y in the co-rotating frame) and velocity with sliders; each change re-runs the simulation, and a reset zeroes all offsets
features.specific: Position trim (Move in/out adds to x, Move sideways adds to y, ±1.5 separations) and Velocity trim (Nudge move, ±1). Per the code the trims add into the initial state. Each change re-runs a three-period REBOUND forecast. ↺ 'Recenter probe and zero the perturbations' zeroes the trims.
steps: Select the target Lagrange point
Drag one or more of Move in/out, Move sideways and Nudge move
Wait for the rerun
Press ↺ to zero the perturbations before the next trial
serves_tasks: Offset the test body's starting state from the equilibrium point
Offset the test body's starting position along the x-axis of the co-rotating frame
Offset the test body's starting position along the y-axis of the co-rotating frame
Give the test body an initial velocity offset
Compare bounded versus escaping behaviour across equilibrium points and systems

features.name: Run summary readout
features.general: A strip of summary numbers for the current run (largest excursion from the start point, a conserved energy-like quantity, mass ratio and period), shown under every view and refreshed on each rerun so trials can be compared
features.specific: Telemetry readout under Mission data: Max deviation (labelled AU, but in units of the separation), Jacobi constant (one value per run), Mass ratio (μ), Orbital period ('3 orbital periods'). It appears only after a Lagrange point is selected.
steps: Select a Lagrange point so the readout appears
Read Max deviation, Jacobi constant, μ and Orbital period
Change a setting and compare the new values
serves_tasks: Read summary numbers for the run
Compare bounded versus escaping behaviour across equilibrium points and systems

features.name: Multi-mode trajectory viewer (animated / 2D map / 3D potential surface)
features.general: Show the same simulated path three ways: an animation, a flat plot with coordinate hover and zoom, and a 3D energy landscape with value hover and camera rotation
features.specific: Display layers radio (Cinematic, 2D Map, 3D Terrain) switches the Plotly figure. Cinematic animates the rotating system. 2D Map draws the rotating-frame path with contour rings and (x, y) hover. 3D Terrain draws the effective-potential surface with the path on it and x/y/potential hover. The standard Plotly toolbar gives zoom, pan, orbit, reset, autoscale and PNG download; in the replay, Reset axes did not seem to restore the 2D view but Autoscale did.
steps: Choose Cinematic, 2D Map or 3D Terrain
Hover the path or surface for coordinates or potential
Box-zoom (2D) or orbit-rotate (3D)
Reset axes or camera (or Autoscale)
serves_tasks: View the whole path in the co-rotating frame and probe coordinates
See the path on the energy surface that governs it
Save a picture of the current figure

features.name: Time-step playback scrubber
features.general: Replay a time series: play/pause, a step slider to scrub to any frame, and a speed multiplier
features.specific: ▶/Ⅱ button, ⚙ Timeline button that shows a step-0…step-N slider, and a speed menu (0.25X–10X) inside the orbital plot. In Cinematic mode the frame rotates; in 2D Map the satellite marker moves along the drawn path. The slider handle does not follow the marker during playback.
steps: Press ⚙ Timeline to show the step slider
Drag the handle to a step
Open the speed menu and pick a multiplier
Press ▶/Ⅱ to play or pause
